order: Add memory files to the Director's authoring exceptions in the guard hook: the project's root memory file and its local sibling anywhere in the project, user-level memory under the assistant's config directory (that directory's own memory file plus markdown inside memory/memories directories, the auto-memory notebook), and any project-relative path matching a new `directorMemoryPatterns` knob in orchestra.json. Memory distills the conversation only the Director holds, and blocking it breaks the built-in auto-memory. Document the exception in the protocol and the README, and reuse the plan carve-out's containment discipline: resolved paths, traversal-checked, nothing outside the project or the config directory. Fence the exception with exactly one rule — simulate each write (Write / Edit / MultiEdit semantics) and deny any result that does not carry the whole managed ORCHESTRA:BEGIN / ORCHESTRA:END block through byte-for-byte; surviving marker lines are not sufficient evidence, the text between them must come through intact too. Keep the denial model-aware and leave every non-memory path blocked as it is today. Separately add harness versioning: a VERSION file at the master root as the single source of truth, stamped by the installer into the installed protocol header and surfaced by /orchestra-status. Do not change the version format.
claims: The exception covers only the project memory files, config-directory memory, and `directorMemoryPatterns` matches; every other path still falls to default law. The managed block rides through every permitted memory write byte-for-byte — the write is simulated and the result denied unless the block survives unchanged, so markers alone cannot buy an edit through. The denial is model-aware; dormant sessions never see it. Version format unchanged (X.Y.Z), read from the VERSION file only. Verified against the 22-case hook matrix plus an install/re-install/uninstall round-trip.
